content.intro: Learn admin security and limitations through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Admin Security and Limitations matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines admin security and limitations as part of django admin. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

items.title: Testing custom admin permissions
items.text: Model permissions are a useful starting point but do not automatically enforce ownership of every individual record. Scope each lookup and mutation to the caller’s authorized objects.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
